headline: Pakistan's first astronaut flies on a Chinese rocket

sources.title: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying 2 Chinese and a Pakistani astronaut (AP, on CNA)
China's Shenzhou-24 space flight takes off with Pakistani national as first foreign astronaut (Reuters, on The Straits Times)
Shenzhou 24: Pakistan's first astronaut goes to space aboard Chinese rocket (BBC)
Pakistani astronaut carries 'hopes of 250 million' on China space mission (AFP, on CNA)

chunks.text: On the morning of November 25, 2026, a Chinese rocket {{lifted off}} from a [[launch center]] in northwest China. Hundreds of people gathered before dawn to {{see the crew off}}. [[On board]] were two Chinese astronauts and a 40-year-old pilot from Pakistan's [[air force]]. He became the first person from Pakistan to [[reach orbit]], or circle Earth in space. About three and a half hours later, the [[spacecraft]] reached China's [[space station]], a large lab in space. The pilot became its first foreign visitor.

chunks.text: China and Pakistan have long been [[close partners]]. In February 2025, they signed an [[agreement]] that {{set up}} this flight. It was the first time Chinese astronauts {{teamed up}} with a foreign astronaut on a Chinese mission. The Pakistani pilot {{went through}} seven months of [[intensive training]] in China's capital. The Chinese crew leader said working across languages and cultures was hard, but both sides' [[efforts]] were {{paying off}}.

Studying every day pays off at test time. Her long hours at the gym pay off in every race. The Chinese crew leader said both sides' efforts were paying off.

chunks.text: The pilot flew as a [[payload specialist]], a [[crew member]] whose main job is science work. He was set to stay five to 10 days. The crew planned to {{carry out}} more than 90 [[experiments]] and tests. His work included a study of tiny living things that make their food from sunlight. His plan was to {{come back}} to Earth with two members of the crew already on the station. Chinese astronauts usually stay about six months.

chunks.text: China was {{kept out}} of the International Space Station, led by NASA, the U.S. [[space agency]]. In 2011, the U.S. [[banned]] NASA from working with China. China then {{put together}} a space station of its own. It wants other countries to use it for research. The international station could be {{shut down}} by 2030. Only the U.S., China and Russia have sent people into space on their own spacecraft.

mainIdea.s: A Pakistani air force pilot flew into orbit on a Chinese rocket, the first person from his country to do so. He also became the first foreign visitor to China's own space station.
mainIdea.why: The rocket lifted off on November 25, 2026. The pilot was set to stay for five to 10 days and carry out science work.

mainIdea.s: Pakistan used a rocket of its own to send two of its pilots into space for six months. They planned to live and work on a Chinese station under a deal the countries signed in early 2025.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the rocket was Chinese, only one Pakistani pilot flew, and he planned a short stay. The other pilot trained in China but did not fly on this mission.

mainIdea.s: China said it will add a fourth large part to its space station next year to make room for more crews. The new part is meant to hold extra labs for tests in medicine and materials.
mainIdea.why: This story is about Pakistan's first astronaut lifting off on a Chinese rocket to visit China's space station.

tf.s: A Pakistani pilot became the first person from Pakistan to reach orbit.

tf.why: He went through seven months of intensive training in China's capital.

tf.why: He flew as a payload specialist, and the crew planned to carry out more than 90 experiments and tests.

tf.s: China helped build the International Space Station.
tf.why: China was kept out of that station, and then it put together a space station of its own.

tf.s: The Pakistani pilot planned to come back to Earth after a short stay.
tf.why: He was set to stay five to 10 days and come back with two members of the crew already there.

lines.text: Did you hear that Pakistan has its first astronaut?
I did. His rocket {{lifted off}} from China on November 25.
Hundreds of people gathered before dawn to {{see the crew off}}.
And a few hours later, he became the first foreign visitor to China's space station.
How did a Pakistani pilot get a seat on a Chinese rocket?
A 2025 deal {{set up}} the flight. It was the first time Chinese astronauts {{teamed up}} with a foreign one.
Did he have to learn Chinese?
Yes. He {{went through}} seven months of training in Beijing, and he said the language was the hardest part.
He worked hard [[every step of the way]].
The crew leader said both sides' efforts were {{paying off}}. [[Two heads are better than one]].
What was his job in space?
He flew as a payload specialist, so his job was to help {{carry out}} experiments.
How long was he going to stay on the station?
Just five to 10 days. Maybe a longer trip is [[in the cards]] someday.
So his visit was [[short and sweet]]. He was set to {{come back}} with two of the crew already there.
Why does China have its own station, anyway?
It was {{kept out}} of the International Space Station in 2011, so it {{put together}} its own.
And the international one could be {{shut down}} by 2030. Kids in Pakistan can now [[reach for the stars]].
